title: Build the alignment matrix and a copy decoder
brief: Stack the attention weights of every decoder step into an alignment matrix, hand-set a scorer so each step reads the right source position, and compare it with an order-blind summary.
hints: alignment_matrix calls additive_attention once per query and stacks the results: contexts with np.stack, weights as the rows of A.
mean_summary is the mean of the one-hot rows of np.eye(vocab_size)[source_tokens]. Shuffling the tokens cannot change it.
For decode_with_attention, use queries = keys = 10 * np.eye(T), values = one-hot rows for the source tokens, W1 = W2 = np.eye(T), and v = v_sign * 10 * np.ones(T).
Read the decoded token as int(np.argmax(context)) for each row of contexts. With v_sign = +1 the matching key scores lower than the others, so the diagonal of the alignment falls to nearly zero.
